name: AI-native software development
summary: Coding assistants and agents help write, test, review and maintain software throughout the development process.
useCase: A developer asks an assistant to update an API client, generate regression tests and open a proposed change for review.
whyNow: Developer tools combine access to source code, execution environments and feedback from tests, making software an unusually measurable AI application. Microsoft reported more than one million paid GitHub Copilot users in late 2023 and 1.8 million in 2024. Its later 20-million-user disclosure includes a broader audience, so it must not be treated as paid-subscriber growth.

mainstream.scope: Supervised AI assistance in professional software teams, with testing and accountable human review.
mainstream.rationale: The product category has paying users, mature distribution and fast feedback. In the 2026 McKinsey survey, coding-agent scaling was already material among large organizations. The forecast concerns routine assistance and bounded delegated changes; autonomous ownership of complex software systems remains much less certain.

metric.name: Paid GitHub Copilot users — company proxy
metric.scope: Microsoft-reported GitHub Copilot paying users, dated snapshots.
metric.limitations: The starting point is a lower bound and snapshot timing differs. Microsoft’s 20 million total users in 2025 includes a different population and is excluded from this paid series. Subscriber counts do not establish engineering productivity or software quality.
metric.futureNote: No defensible same-definition subscriber forecast is supplied. Future gains should be judged by shipped, reliable software per engineer, not generated lines of code.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: GitHub introduced Copilot as an AI pair-programming technical preview.
The paid-user time series is unavailable here; no interpolated adoption count is inserted.
Microsoft reported more than one million paid GitHub Copilot users in October.
The Microsoft annual report reported 1.8 million paid users.
Microsoft reported 20 million total Copilot users, a definition break from paid subscribers.
McKinsey found growing large-company coding-agent deployment; Cursor became part of SpaceX in August.

tailwinds: Code repositories, tests and build systems provide machine-readable feedback.
AI lowers the cost of repetitive maintenance, prototypes and migration work.
bottlenecks: Generated changes can introduce subtle security, reliability and licensing problems.
Review capacity, context quality and test coverage can become the bottleneck as code output rises.
watchMetrics: Lead time to a deployed change alongside escaped defects and rework.
Cost per accepted change and the share of agent proposals that pass meaningful tests and review.
